On Fri, 28 Jul 2028 at 15:05, Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@auroraedge.com> wrote:
> Attached is our initial network CIDR plan (auroraedge-vpc-cidr-plan.xlsx). Can Redwood confirm:
> - Preferred peering architecture (direct VPC peering vs transit gateway) for high throughput?
> - Supported TLS termination model for private endpoints?
> - On-prem installer options (air-gapped tarball vs registry pull)?

Thanks Aisha — quick technical notes from our infra engineering side:
- Transit gateway vs direct peering: if you expect multi-region ingress or multiple VPCs (control + workloads), TGW is easier to scale. For single-VPC high-throughput, direct peering reduces hop count and simplifies MTU. We can support either; we just need the peering ASN and route tables.
- MTU and jumbo frames: please confirm if your DC uses jumbo frames; our appliance can be configured but we need to know before testing.
- TCP keepalive & idle timeouts: some transit gateways have aggressive idle timeouts — we'll run a syn/keepalive test during the preflight.
- TLS/mTLS: Redwood supports mTLS for private endpoints. If you choose mTLS we will need an intermediary CA or agreed cert rotation cadence.
- NAT & egress: if peering is one-way (ingress only), you may require a NAT gateway for our health checks.
- DNS: recommend split-horizon DNS with a private hosted zone; we can provide the endpoint hostnames to add.
- KMS: if you use customer KMS, provide the KMS key ARN and the contact for IAM policies.

Action items for network team before kickoff:
- Provide peering ASN and route table snippets
- Confirm MTU and firewall egress/ingress policy windows
- Confirm public IPs for allowlist (we will provide our set)

I'll bring a short runbook for the staging peering test.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

From: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@auroraedge.com>

Thanks, Marissa and Dylan — good notes. Please find answers inline and the updated CIDR workbook attached.

- Peering: we'll prefer direct VPC peering for the primary cluster (single VPC model). We will use TGW for cross-account routing in future phases.
- ASN & routes: ASN 64522; primary route table will advertise 10.41.0.0/16 for workloads.
- MTU: we support jumbo frames (9001).
- TLS: we'll start with Redwood-managed certs for speed, then transition to mTLS for production.
- KMS & SSO: we use Vault-backed CMKs. Contact for KMS/IAM is network.ops@auroraedge.com.
- On-prem installer: procurement has requested an air-gapped tarball for the appliance; procurement@auroraedge.com is copied.

I'll attach the latest workbook (auroraedge-vpc-cidr-plan.xlsx) with the specific subnets we'll reserve for the appliance. Procurement will start the approval for the hardware spec.

Next steps: confirm a peering test window Tues 2028-08-01 17:00-19:00 UTC. Can Redwood commit one engineer for the window?

Best,
Aisha
